recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If tighter current MolecularDefinition strand terminology is needed, handle it as a new MolecularDefinition-specific Clinical Genomics issue rather than replaying retired Sequence wording.
issue_request: FHIR-11237 was a Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics change request against DSTU2 FHIR-core Sequence. It said Sequence.referenceSeq.strand was an integer and should be more constrained, with final resolution text explaining +1 as plus strand (5' to 3')/Watson/Sense/positive and -1 as minus strand (3' to 5')/Crick/Antisense/negative.
initial_application: No historical commit explicitly names FHIR-11237, but the same strand-change family was applied to the old Sequence source: commit 6072b705b61538f2fe3fe5d5cc3779298ae2e79c revised the Sequence.referenceSeq.strand definition for FHIR-11238, and commit a26b8894d0c1ab993ffd7d6d0e4d4d0e4ba40c27 added Sequence notes with the +1/-1 mapping that matches FHIR-11237's resolution.
additional_context: Later Clinical Genomics work changed the same area: ed2a92ec7970500700c90a1d576a6dd9963fcdc0 split the old strand semantics into watson/crick strand plus sense/antisense orientation, FHIR-19453 renamed Sequence to MolecularSequence, and later R6 work replaced MolecularSequence with MolecularDefinition. Current fhir.ini lists Sequence under removed resources, comments MolecularSequence out of current metadata, and makes moleculardefinition the active Clinical Genomics resource. The current MolecularDefinition strand element is a different CodeableConcept element.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reapplying the old +1/-1 integer guidance to current MolecularDefinition would be outside FHIR-11237's historical build scope and would conflict with later model changes rather than completing the published issue.
